source.name: ASTRA Bio wave 1 — Plant Ecology
source.license: Original syllabus-based practice questions (exam-frequent themes; not verbatim past papers)

questions.stem: The branch of ecology that studies a single species in relation to its environment is
questions.explanation: Autecology is species-level ecology; synecology deals with communities and ecosystems.

questions.stem: The physical place where an organism lives is its habitat, whereas its functional role is its
questions.explanation: Habitat is the address; the niche is the profession — resources used and interactions performed.

questions.stem: Among climatic factors, photoperiod mainly influences
questions.explanation: Day length is a climatic cue that induces flowering in short-day and long-day plants.

questions.stem: Soil texture, pH and mineral content are grouped as
questions.explanation: Edaphic factors are soil properties; slope and altitude are topographic.

questions.stem: Aerenchyma that creates air channels in stems and roots is a hallmark of many
questions.explanation: Aquatic plants develop aerenchyma for buoyancy and oxygen movement through submerged organs.

questions.stem: Sunken stomata overarched by hairs are a typical anatomical feature of
questions.explanation: Sunken stomata sit in pits that trap humid air and cut transpiration in dry habitats.

questions.stem: Vivipary, in which seeds germinate on the parent plant, is well known in
questions.explanation: Many mangroves show vivipary so seedlings are established before they drop into saline mud.

questions.stem: The transition zone between two adjacent communities is called an
questions.explanation: An ecotone is the edge community; species richness is often high there (edge effect).

questions.stem: Primary succession on bare rock typically begins with
questions.explanation: Lichens weather rock and add organic matter, starting a xerosere toward a climax community.

questions.stem: Mycorrhizal association between a fungus and a plant root is an example of
questions.explanation: The fungus gains carbon and the plant gains mineral uptake; both partners benefit.

questions.stem: Plants that complete their life cycle in the brief wet spell of a desert and persist as seeds are
questions.explanation: Desert ephemerals avoid drought as dormant seeds rather than enduring it as vegetative plants.

questions.stem: Secondary succession differs from primary succession mainly because it starts on
options: sterile bare rock with no soil
a site that already has soil after a disturbance
questions.explanation: Fire, flood or abandonment leaves soil and propagules, so secondary seres proceed faster.

questions.stem: Choose the correct set. I. Synecology studies groups of organisms. II. A hydrosere begins in water and may end in a forest climax. III. Halophytes always lack any salt-excreting glands.
questions.explanation: Community ecology and hydrosere are correctly stated; many mangroves have salt glands or succulent leaves.

questions.stem: Synecology is best defined as the study of
options: one organism in isolation from all others
communities and their interactions with the environment
mineral deficiency symptoms of a single crop
questions.explanation: Synecology (community ecology) deals with groups of species and their environment.

questions.stem: Two plant species can share a habitat yet avoid competitive exclusion if they occupy
questions.explanation: Gause’s idea: complete niche overlap leads to exclusion; niche differentiation allows coexistence.

questions.stem: Wind as a climatic factor is especially important for
options: producing annual rings in roots only
questions.explanation: Wind pollinates many grasses and trees and also carries winged or plumed diaspores.

questions.stem: Altitude and slope aspect that change local climate are classified as
questions.explanation: Topography (height, slope, aspect) modifies temperature, rainfall and insolation.

questions.stem: Highly dissected or finely divided leaves in submerged aquatics mainly help to
options: reduce the surface available for gas exchange
increase surface area and reduce tearing by currents
store starch in amyloplasts of the fruit
questions.explanation: Filamentous submerged leaves raise the exchange surface and flex with flowing water.

questions.stem: Succulent xerophytes such as Opuntia store water chiefly in
questions.explanation: Succulents accumulate water in parenchyma of swollen stems (cladodes) or leaves.

questions.stem: Mesophytes are plants that grow typically in
questions.explanation: Mesophytes occupy mesic sites; they lack the extreme aerenchyma of hydrophytes or the strong xeromorphy of xerophytes.

questions.stem: Vertical layering of vegetation in a forest (trees, shrubs, herbs) is called
questions.explanation: Stratification is the vertical structure of a community; zonation is horizontal banding.

questions.stem: The relatively stable end community of a sere is the
questions.explanation: Succession proceeds through seral stages to a self-replacing climax under the regional climate.

questions.stem: An epiphyte such as an orchid growing on a tree without parasitising it illustrates
questions.explanation: The epiphyte gains a perch; the tree is typically neither helped nor harmed (commensalism).

questions.stem: Which statement about hydrophytes is incorrect?
options: Submerged leaves may be highly dissected.
They typically possess a very thick, multi-layered cuticle and dense sunken stomata on submerged leaves.
questions.explanation: Submerged organs usually have a thin cuticle and lack stomata; sunken stomata are a xerophyte trait.

questions.stem: A hydrosere in a freshwater pond is expected to pass from submerged plants toward
options: floating, then reed-swamp and woodland stages
a purely plankton climax with no rooted plants ever
questions.explanation: A classic hydrosere: submerged → floating → reed swamp → marsh → woodland climax as the basin fills.

questions.stem: Identify the incorrect pairing.
options: Xerosere — succession starting on dry bare rock
Halophyte — plant confined to permanently dark caves
questions.explanation: Halophytes inhabit saline soils or waters; cave plants are shade/sciophytes, not defined by salt.
